conventions.hubs: An add-on is turned on per account and adds a monthly base fee. Add-ons stack at full price; each includes what every add-on includes, so a business app never needs the Consumer Identity add-on for its branding.
conventions.user_meters: Monthly active users are never billed, and requiring MFA never counts a user. The Consumer Identity add-on counts social users: a user who signs in through an external identity provider set up on a project and not linked to a team, once a month. Password, passkey, magic-link and OTP sign-ins never count. An identity provider linked to a team is an SSO connection, counted by Multi-Tenancy, never twice.
conventions.tiers: Two tiers: Pay as you go and Enterprise. Pay as you go starts free with no card, with every core feature and a free amount on most meters; add-ons go on top. Billing keeps two plan ids for it: free while no add-on is on, pro once one is.
conventions.allowance: Every meter Pay as you go offers before an add-on has a free amount. Turning on the meter's add-on raises it to the add-on's included amount; past that, the price applies.
conventions.invoice: base fees of the add-ons turned on + usage past the add-ons' included amounts + extra capacity and support; nothing is billed while no add-on is on
conventions.caps: Owners set a monthly budget and get alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent of it; it notifies and never stops sign-ins or switches security enforcement off.
conventions.capacity: API requests are never billed. Each project has a rate limit; owners add capacity in steps, which raise every project's limit.
conventions.self_hosted: Self-hosted works like the cloud, under a dual license: everything Pay as you go includes before an add-on is free under the AGPL, and add-ons take the same base fees and meters under a commercial license. The installation counts its own usage and reports it monthly. A modified or patched build keeps its AGPL rights but loses warranty, support and any SLA. Air-gapped installations agree an annual true-up in an Enterprise contract.

free.label: Pay as you go
free.over_allowance: Nothing is billed until an add-on is on, and no add-on turns on by itself. Owners get an email and a console banner at 50, 80 and 100 percent of each free amount, with the price of the add-on that lifts it. The first month past a free amount, nothing stops. From the next month, a meter still past its free amount without its add-on holds new usage there: a social user or SSO connection not yet counted that month can't start, and token exchanges past it are refused. Everyone already counted that month keeps signing in, and users, passwords, passkeys and MFA never stop.
